annotations.shape: one text/plain us-ascii message with a NUL byte inside a header VALUE (`X-Nul: be\x00fore`); the field name is well formed, so the field still parses (parse_status ok) and the raw value keeps the NUL
annotations.raw_fixture: hand-written bytes in tools/write_raw_fixtures.py, frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS -- a NUL byte in a value is exactly what a text generator cannot emit
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, headers.fields (the NUL is in the value, so the field is ordinal 3 with parse_status ok and the raw value ' be\x00fore'), part.tree, part.regions, part.gaps, body.preamble_epilogue, decode.chain and body.content_sha256
annotations.phase_1_facts: headers.projection (a NUL in a value is recorded, not repaired) and document.axes
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the RFC and design rules (D2/D9), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: a field's raw_span covers its line including the line ending; value_span starts immediately after the colon and keeps the leading space and the NUL byte
annotations.expected_gaps: none: a NUL in a value is not a malformed line (the NAME is what must be well formed), so headers.malformed_line does not fire
annotations.not_yet_labelled: addresses, the Date projection, encoded words, body views, attachments, statuses, thread edges and TimeEvents
